answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is stake-weighted identity with slow onboarding. Each agent locks collateral that is forfeited if its peers flag fraudulent attestations, so one operator cannot cheaply spin up thousands of identities. New agents start with low trust and earn weight gradually, like a glacier carving a valley over years rather than overnight. Reputation compounds only through verified work, so a spiral of fake activity becomes expensive to sustain. Reaching full standing is a summit, not a shortcut.
